newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Randgold Resources details resource base.
newsitem.headline: Randgold Resources details resource base.

text.p: Randgold Resources Ltd said on Monday it had defined a resource base of nine million ounces in four countries and was evaluating several new discoveries.
The company, which is active in west and central Africa, said this followed the takeover of BHP Minerals Mali, including the Syama Gold Mine, its first gold mine, in October last year.

The takeover of the BHP unit had proceeded smoothly and the potential value of the other assets acquired from BHP confirmed, Randgold Resources said in a statement accompanying its December quarter results.

Mark Bristow, managing director of the firm, said management was paying particular attention to improving Syama's gold yield, introducing new mining practices, establishing better labour relations and upgrading plant and equipment.

He said $39 million would be needed over the next 24 months to expand mining equipment fleet, and to improve mineral processing operations and the mine's infrastructure. He said this would be financed from profits and bank loans.
Randgold Resources said it had acquired three new prospecting licences in the Ivory Coast.

At the Golden Ridge project in Tanzania a measured and indicated reserve of 12.39 million tonnes at a grade of 2.54 g/t for a total of 1.01 million ounces of gold has been estimated to 100m depth. A decision on a full bankable feasibility study would be made in July, Randgold Resources said.
Exploration programmes at its other properties in west and central Africa, where a total of 217 targets have been identified, continued, it said.
